Container.Name: curator
Container.Overview:
Curates the art on Samsung's The Frame TVs: upload pictures to a TV, browse and choose what it shows, group pieces into albums and have a TV rotate through one on a schedule, and back it all up as a zip. A web app on your home network, with no sign-in, so keep it there.
The web app and its API share one port. The database schema is applied at every start, so updating the container is all an upgrade takes.
It waits up to a minute for the database at start, so it can boot alongside your Postgres container, and it takes ownership of its Data folder as nobody:users, Unraid's usual owner.
First run: open the web app, go to TVs, and search for your Frame (or add it by its address). The TV shows a pairing prompt; accept it with the remote. Give each TV a DHCP reservation, because a TV is remembered by its address.
Host networking is the default because the TVs page finds Frames by SSDP multicast, which Docker's bridge network does not pass. On bridge everything else works; add each TV by address.
Container.Requires: A PostgreSQL server (17 is what curator is tested on; no extensions needed). Curator creates its database there on first start, given a user allowed to create databases. An x86-64 server: there is no arm64 image.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: The web app, with its API under /api. On host networking (the default) nothing is mapped: the container listens on Port below itself, so keep the two the same and make sure nothing else on the server uses it. On bridge this is the host port mapped to the container's 14100.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The originals of every picture you upload (a TV keeps only its own resized copy and cannot hand the full image back) and the app's log. Everything else is in the database, so back up both. Owned by the user and group below; the container sets that itself at start.

Config.Name: Database host
Config.Description: Your PostgreSQL server. For a Postgres container on this server, the server's own address (such as 192.168.1.10) with Postgres's port published: a container name does not resolve from host networking.

Config.Name: Database name
Config.Description: Created at first start if it does not exist, which needs a user allowed to create databases (the postgres superuser is). With a user that is not, create it first (CREATE DATABASE curator OWNER that_user). Its tables are created and updated at every start.

Config.Name: Database user
Config.Description: Applies the schema at every start, so it needs to create tables in the database, and to create the database itself if it does not exist yet.

Config.Name: Port
Config.Description: The port the app listens on inside the container. Only worth changing on host networking when 14100 is taken; set WebUI above to the same number so the WebUI link follows.

Config.Name: User ID
Config.Description: Who the app runs as, and who owns everything it writes to Data. 99 is nobody, which is what the rest of appdata belongs to on Unraid. The container makes Data theirs at start if it is not already.

Config.Name: Group ID
Config.Description: The group for the same: 100 is users.
